about:
Micro-Tek Corporation operates from a 30,000-square-foot facility in Cinnaminson, New Jersey. The company was founded in 1965 by George Rogers as the Miniature Insulated Wire Company and incorporated under its current name in 1966. Now under third-generation family ownership, the business has grown from a small shop into a multi-generational manufacturer serving aerospace, medical, and industrial markets worldwide.

Micro-Tek specializes in custom drawing, flattening, stranding, insulating, cutting, and stripping of fine wire and cable down to .0009 inch (AWG #50). Its capabilities include PTFE fluoropolymer extrusion for coax cores, tubing, and cables; etching for bondability on PTFE, FEP, PFA, and ETFE; wire winding; and contract manufacturing. All processes—wire drawing, stranding, insulating, and tubing—are performed under one roof, supporting custom and short runs as well as high-volume production.

The company serves aerospace customers with micro-coaxial cable, shielded twisted pair cable, and high-performance coaxial core for avionics, satellite systems, and communication equipment. In the medical sector, it supplies PTFE coaxial core, flat wire, fluoropolymer tubing, and etched liners for surgical devices, diagnostic imaging, braiding, coiling, and sensors. Industrial clients use its custom wire and cable for automation systems and high-temperature manufacturing processes requiring chemical resistance and durability.

Micro-Tek emphasizes precision, holding tolerances as fine as ±0.0002 inch, and flexibility, offering small runs, large orders, and just-in-time or contract manufacturing. The company cites its decades of experience, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and long-term customer relationships as key differentiators.
